AFTERNOON SESSION-Thur sday, October 11, 1984
Members and guests assembled at 2:00 P.M. for the Open Installation
of the Officers elected and appointed to serve for the ensuing Grand
Lodge year, Grand Master E . Arthur Haglund presiding .

275

The Installation Ceremony commenced at 2:00 P.M ., with the retiring
Grand Master, E .. Arthur Haglund , acting as Installing Officer, and Past
Grand Master Kermit A. Jacobson acting as Master of Ceremonies . In
accordance with Ritual , all of the Appointive Officers were duly installed
after which the Grand Lecturer, Grand Secretary and Grand Treasurer
were installed . The Junior Grand Warden and Senior Grand Warden were
then installed in their respective stations. The Deputy Grand Master was
then installed after which the Grand Master was duly installed .
The newly installed Grand Master expressed his appreciation to the
Installing Officer and the Master of Ceremonies for their parts in the
lnstaJJation Ceremony. He then presented the retiring Grand Lodge Officers and their ladies who were accorded a standing ovation in appreciation of a most successful Masonic year just completed . The newly installed
Grand Master requested the Grand Marshal to escort the wife of the
Junior Past Grand Master, Barbara Jean, to the East whereupon Past
Grand Master Robert 0. West presented her with a gift on behalf of the
entire membership for her love and devotion to the Fraternity as its First
Lady. This lovely lady expressed her appreciation for this thoughtful consideration and remembrance . Affectionately known as " Barbie ," she was
then presented with a beautiful bouquet of red roses by Grand Master
Henville who then presented the Junior Past Grand Master and his lady
Barbara to the audience who greeted them with a standing ovation of
thanks for a job well done .
Past Grand Master Vernon L. Gordon presented the Past Grand Master's lapel pin to the retiring Grand Master. Past Grand Master Robert 0 .
West presented the J\1nior Past Grand Master with the Past Grand Master's
apron , and the Senior Past Grand Master, Edward H . Siems, presented
Brother Haglund with the Past Grand Master's Certificate. The retiring
Grand Master met with the newly installed Grand Master, the Deputy
Grand Master and the Senior and Junior Grand Wardens at the Altar
where they exchanged the Arthur S. Crites lapel pins of their respective
offices. Appropriate words of fraternal fellowship accompanied each of
the presentations .
The Grand Master introduced the staff of the Grand Lodge Office. the
guests from the Masonic Home in Union City who were in attendance and
the Appointive Officers and their ladies . The Elective Officers introduced
their ladies after which the Grand Master recognized the members of San
Marino Lodge No. 685 and their ladies who were in attendance. Sandor
Bory, Master of San Marino Lodge No. 685. presented a sculptured bust
of Grand Master Henville that represented a gift of respect, dedication
and l;>rotherly love. Grand Master Henville presented his charming wife
Elinor and other members of his family.
The newly installed Grand Master addressed the audience stating that
there are many things to be accomplished . His being elected to serve as
Grand Master was both a challenge and an honor. Success can only be

achieved with tremendous cooperation and support from the membership
throughout the entire year. The Brethren of the Craft were encouraged
to come forward at any time and offer their suggestions or receive counsel
and advice as the door to the Grand Master's Office , and his heart , are
always open to the Brethre n. It is most important that all of us proceed
with the proper attitude, and what we do or do not do should be scrutinized by o urselves and others , and each one of us should be accountable
to ourselves and to others for our actions. Grand Master He nville expressed his sincerity, honesty and the gratitude that was in his heart for
being accorded the opportunity to serve the Frate rnity as Grand Master.
Upon completion of his remarks the Grand Maste r received a standing
ovation .
Special thanks were extended to Organist James C. Myers and Soloist
Davis B. Leonard for their beautiful musical selections , "No Man ls An

NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES:
NOTE 1 - SUHMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES:
The financial statements of Masonic Homes of California have been
prepared on the accrual basis of accounting.
Significant accounting
policies follow:
Fund Accounting:
To insure observance of limitations and restrictions placed on the
use of resources available to the Homes, the accounts of the Homes are
maintained in accordance with the principles of fund accounting.
The assets, liabilities and fund balances of the Homes are reported
in four self-balancing funds, as follow:
General Fund - Resources are available to support the operations of
the Homes at Union City and Covina, California.
Permanent Endowment Fund - Ordinances of the Grand Lodge provide that
no portion of the principal of the Permanent Endowment Fund shall be
expended for any purpose and income from the pr lncipal shall be used
only for the maintenance and general operation of Masonic Homes.
Hugo M. Lorber Masonic Home, Union City Fund - This fund provides for
the operation, preservation and betterment of the Home at Union City,
California.
Restricted Trust Funds - Details to these Trust Funds are contained
in Note 7 to the financial statements.
Investments in Securities:
Investments, consisting of marketable securities, are stated at fair
market values.
Changes in market values between reporting dates are
recognized for financial reporting.

Depreciation ls recorded
following estimated lives:

by

the

(Concluded)

Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense when incurred.
Betterments of a major nature which extend the useful lives of buildings
and equipment are capitalized.
On sale or retirement, the cost and
accumulated depreciation applicable thereto are eliminated from the
accounts and the differences between net book value and the proceeds from
sale or retlrment are included in income.
Other Assets:
Other assets consist of life insurance policies, real estate and
mineral rights assigned or bequeathed to the Masonic Homes.
Real estate and mineral rights are recorded at the nominal value of
$1 each for accountability. Payments by the Masonic Homes of obligations
of the assignors secured by these assets are added to the nominal value.
Life insurance policies are recorded at their actuarily determined
present values.

NOT E 6 - HUGO H. LORBER MASONIC HOME, UNION CITY FUND :
During 1982 and 1983, the Maso nic Homes of California received
beques ts from the Estate of Hugo H. Lorber ln the amount of $11,680, 365 .
Hr. Lorber's Last Will and Testament provided that the bequest be used at
the Home for the elderly at Union Clty, California.
The Board of Trustees established the Hugo H. Lorber Masoni c Home,
Union City Fund t o account for the bequest and resolved that all income
from the Fund should be used for operating, rehabilitatin g, preserving
and e nhanc ing the Home for Adults at Union City, as deemed necessary.
The Board of Trustees also resolved that the Fund r ep r ese nted a
source for additions and replacements of property at Union Clty, as
represented •by the accumulatiOfl of depreciation .
